sections.what_happened: Iran's offer to the US to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days remains on the table. Iran presented the proposal in mid-September after an interim ceasefire collapsed; Tehran acknowledged receiving a US response, but Iran's security chief said last week negotiations stalled because Washington failed to address all seven conditions for reopening the strait.
sections.what_verified: Reuters-cited attribution; mid-September proposal and collapsed interim ceasefire referenced in multiple wires; seven conditions referenced but not enumerated in available reporting — details unverified.
sections.what_disputed: No US-side confirmation of the offer's current status in this reporting window.
sections.why_matters: While a third tanker burns, Tehran says it will reopen the strait in 7 days — if Washington meets seven conditions. What are the conditions, and who is actually blocking the deal?
sections.context: Background: Hormuz diplomacy — Iran's 7-day Strait of Hormuz reopening offer still on the table (Araghchi via Reuters); talks stalled on seven US conditions

totw_analysis: Our read: While a third tanker burns, Tehran says it will reopen the strait in 7 days — if Washington meets seven conditions. What are the conditions, and who is actually blocking the deal? The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is Iran's reopening offer a genuine exit ramp — or a ceasefire-bait trap while the mines keep hitting tankers?
